value.rationale: Ordinal equivalence of Shapley–Shubik and Banzhaf is an established structural question in voting power. The complete first layer is naturally motivated by the known six-player threshold, and the zero-reversal theorem reveals a rigid qualitative phenomenon: first disagreement arises only by Shapley–Shubik resolving Banzhaf ties. The proper and dummy-free subresults show that this is not a degenerate artifact.
